2608.19689.title: Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
2608.19689.paper_summary: LLM-based social simulation is a promising complement to traditional methods such as surveys and behavioral experiments. A core question is how to evaluate the fidelity of LLM-simulated human behavior and optimize LLMs toward it. Prevailing practice evaluates by accuracy, checking whether the model selects the single response observed from a human, and trains the LLM to reproduce this hard label. However, human behavior is inherently subjective: the same person in the same situation may reasonably act differently, so an observed response is only one draw from an underlying response distribution, rendering accuracy-based evaluation unreliable and hard-label training misleading. To address these problems, we first introduce the subjectivity coefficient, an entropy-based quantity distinguishing objective tasks such as coding from subjective ones such as social simulation, and use it to systematically analyze how accuracy-based evaluation and hard-label training fail as subjectivity grows. Based on the subjectivity coefficient, we propose Subjectivity-Adaptive soft-Label Training (SALT): it pools observed outputs from semantically nearby inputs into soft distributional labels, with an aggregation radius adapted to the estimated subjectivity of each input; in the near-objective limit the neighborhood shrinks, so SALT naturally falls back to standard single-label training. Moreover, since existing datasets record only single observed responses and cannot support distributional evaluation, we construct SUBJSIM, a benchmark of 19,300 contexts covering 193 annotators and 100 subjective questions. Since real-world data typically provide only a single observation per input, our experiments train models from single observed outputs while evaluating them against the full response distributions, verifying feasibility in realistic settings. Results on SUBJSIM demonstrate the advantages of our method.
2608.19689.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基礎的社會模擬是傳統方法（如調查和行為實驗）的有前景的補充。<lb/>一個核心問題是如何評估 LLM 模擬的人類行為的真實性並優化 LLM 以達到這一目標。<lb/>目前的做法是通過準確性來評估，檢查模型是否選擇了從人類觀察到的單一反應，並訓練 LLM 重現這一硬標籤。<lb/>然而，人類行為本質上是主觀的：同一人在相同情境中可能會合理地表現出不同的行為，因此觀察到的反應僅僅是潛在反應分布中的一次抽樣，這使得基於準確性的評估不可靠，且硬標籤訓練具有誤導性。<lb/>為了解決這些問題，我們首先引入主觀性係數，這是一種基於熵的量，區分了像編碼這樣的客觀任務和像社會模擬這樣的主觀任務，並利用它系統性地分析隨著主觀性增長，基於準確性的評估和硬標籤訓練如何失敗。<lb/>基於主觀性係數，我們提出了主觀性自適應軟標籤訓練（SALT）：它將來自語義相近輸入的觀察輸出匯聚成軟分佈標籤，聚合半徑根據每個輸入的估計主觀性進行調整；在近乎客觀的極限下，鄰域縮小，因此 SALT 自然回落到標準的單標籤訓練。此外，由於現有數據集僅記錄單一觀察反應，無法支持分佈評估，我們構建了 SUBJSIM，這是一個涵蓋 193 位標註者和 100 個主觀問題的 19,300 個上下文的基準數據集。<lb/>由於現實世界數據通常僅提供每個輸入的單一觀察，我們的實驗從單一觀察輸出訓練模型，同時根據完整的反應分佈進行評估，驗證了在現實環境中的可行性。<lb/>SUBJSIM 上的結果展示了我們方法的優勢。
